question: A shopkeeper lists the price of a fan at 50% above its cost price and offers a 30% discount on its list price. If he earns a profit of ₹175, then what is the list price (in ₹) of the fan?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Cost Price (CP) = 100%. Then List Price (MP) = 150%.

Selling Price (SP) = 150% × (100% − 30%) = 105%.

Profit = SP − CP = 105% − 100% = 5%.

Given, 5% = ₹175 ⇒ 1% = ₹35.

List Price (MP) = 150% = 150 × 35 = 5250.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 CP = 100x
 
 
 SP = 105x

 
 MP = 150x

 

 Mark Up = +50%

 

 Discount = −30%

 

 Profit = +5x
 
 Profit = 5x = ₹175 ⇒ x = 35

**Given:**

Markup Percentage = 50%

Discount Percentage = 30%

Profit = ₹175

**Formula Used:**

List Price (MP) = CP × (1 + Markup% ÷ 100)

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − Discount% ÷ 100)

Profit = SP − CP

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the fan be 100x.

⇒ List Price (MP) = 100x × (1 + 50 ÷ 100) = 150x

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 150x × (1 − 30 ÷ 100) = 150x × 0.7 = 105x

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 105x − 100x = 5x

⇒ We are given that Profit = ₹175, so:

⇒ 5x = 175

⇒ x = 35

⇒ List Price (MP) = 150x = 150 × 35 = 5250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP) and Successive Discounts

MP is the printed or listed price of an item. For successive discounts of a% and b%, Effective Discount = (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Direct Relation between CP and MP

The direct ratio between Cost Price and Marked Price is derived as: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

Dishonest Dealer

When a shopkeeper sells goods at CP but uses false weights, Profit % = (Error ÷ (True Weight − Error)) × 100.
